newsitem.title: GERMANY: German early retirement talks collapse in region.
newsitem.headline: German early retirement talks collapse in region.

text.p: Regional talks between German employers and trade unions in the metal and engineering sector over a scheme to introduce an early retirement plan for workers collapsed on Wednesday, negotiators said.

Representatives from both sides said the talks, in the southern German state of Baden-Wuerttemberg, ended following the failure to come to an agreement. Union representatives threatened possible industrial action.

"If it comes to it, we shall not shy away from industrial action," Gerhard Zambelli, regional head of the IG Metall metal and engineering sector trade union, told reporters after the collapse of the talks.

IG Metall is keen to introduce early retirement clauses into sector-wide wage contracts as part of work redistribution measures it believes will create further employment and training possibilities for young workers in the sector.
Late on Tuesday, car giant Volkswagen AG agreed a scheme that would allow workers effectively to retire at 57-1/2 years instead of the current 60 years.
The region of Baden-Wuerttemberg is home to a number of companies in the sector, including Daimler-Benz AG, which produces the Mercedes range.
